chunks.text: Microscopy Resources and Generalization Evaluation. The Human Protein Atlas ( Thul et al., 2017 ) and OpenCell ( Cho et al., 2022 ) provide annotated protein-localization images, while RxRx1 ( Sypetkowski et al., 2023 ) and Cell Painting resources ( Chandrasekaran et al., 2024 ) capture variation across experimental batches and biological perturbations. MicroPool-2M integrates multiple microscopy sources into a common annotation vocabulary and augments images with three levels of text supervision. Its evaluation distinguishes unseen structures, unseen cell lines, and unseen pairings, complemented by an external source-shift benchmark. The unseen-pair setting relates to compositional zero-shot learning, which evaluates novel combinations of familiar concepts ( Nagarajan and Grauman, 2018 ; Nayak et al., 2023 ) ; unseen-factor evaluation is also studied in open-vocabulary compositional learning ( Saini et al., 2024 ) . We use these distinctions to assess the transfer of microscopy image–text representations alongside language-based retrieval. 4 MicroPool-2M: A Large-Scale Microscopy Image–Text Dataset Motivated by the biological grounding gap identified in Section 3 , we construct MicroPool-2M to provide explicit supervision linking microscopy images to biological semantics. Each fluorescence microscopy image is paired with three complementary levels of text: category-level captions specify its annotated biological identity, knowledge-level captions provide associated biological context, and detail-level captions describe its visible appearance. Together, these captions provide the supervision used to train MicroCLIP to associate biological meaning with microscopy appearance. Image collection and annotation harmonization. Covering diverse biological contexts requires varied image sources and consistent category definitions.

We aggregate single-channel fluorescence images from the Human Protein Atlas ( Thul et al., 2017 ) , Image Data Resource ( Williams et al., 2017 ) , RxRx ( Sypetkowski et al., 2023 ) , Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection ( Ljosa et al., 2012 ) , and curated literature. Source-specific aliases are mapped to a common vocabulary, assigning each image x i x_{i} a structure label s i s_{i} and cell-line identity c i c_{i} . A structure label can denote a single structure or marker, or a combination of them. Each category is represented as e i = ( s i , c i ) e_{i}=(s_{i},c_{i}) . We remove content-identical images before constructing training and evaluation sets. Three-level text supervision. Category labels identify biological entities but do not describe their biological context or the visual appearance of individual images. We therefore pair each image x i x_{i} with category-level, knowledge-level, and detail-level text: t i cat = 𝒯 ⁡ ( s i , c i ) , t i know = Concat ⁡ ( 𝒦 s ​ ( s i ) , 𝒦 c ​ ( c i ) ) , t i det = 𝒟 ⁡ ( x i , e i ) . t_{i}^{\mathrm{cat}}=\mathcal{T}(s_{i},c_{i}),\quad t_{i}^{\mathrm{know}}=\operatorname{Concat}\!\left(\mathcal{K}_{s}(s_{i}),\,\mathcal{K}_{c}(c_{i})\right),\quad t_{i}^{\mathrm{det}}=\mathcal{D}(x_{i},e_{i}). (1) Here, 𝒯 \mathcal{T} applies the category template: a microscopy photo of { structure }_of_{ cell } . The mappings 𝒦 s \mathcal{K}_{s} and 𝒦 c \mathcal{K}_{c} retrieve all available biological descriptions generated by GPT-5.6 Sol for the associated structures or markers and cell line, respectively; composite structure labels include descriptions of all constituent structures. For 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , we prompt Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with the image and the normalized category name corresponding to e i e_{i} to describe fluorescence distribution, morphology, signal intensity, and background. Appendix B provides prompts and caption examples. Dataset coverage.

MicroPool-2M contains 3,301,672 images and 3,391 observed structure–cell-line pairs. After data cleaning and split construction, the training split contains 2,505,017 images spanning 2,032 structure–cell-line categories. The resulting annotations, knowledge tables, and image descriptions define the supervision used by MicroCLIP; the evaluation subsets and protocols are specified in Section 6.1 . Dataset coverage. MicroPool-2M contains 3,301,672 images and 3,391 observed structure–cell-line pairs. After data cleaning and split construction, the training split contains 2,505,017 images spanning 2,032 structure–cell-line categories. The resulting annotations, knowledge tables, and image descriptions define the supervision used by MicroCLIP; the evaluation subsets and protocols are specified in Section 6.1 . 6 Experiments 6.1 Experimental Settings Evaluation data and protocols. We evaluate classification on four MicroPool-2M subsets defined relative to its microscopy training set and summarized in Table 6 . IID contains new images of observed structure–cell-line pairs. Compositional Shift holds out pairs while retaining both constituent labels in training. Cell-Line Shift holds out cell lines while retaining the structure labels, and Organelle-Set Shift holds out complete structure labels while retaining the cell lines. The latter concerns structure labels, which can themselves be composite. Each internal evaluation category contains 100 images. We additionally evaluate Source Shift using 1,158 images from 13 categories drawn from the external Light My Cells dataset (S-BIAD1047) ( Kauffmann et al., 2026 ) . Figure 4 shows representative images from these evaluation settings. For retrieval, we use a held-out pool of 1,000 MicroPool image–text pairs, with each image paired with its detail-level caption. We additionally evaluate zero-shot transfer to projected 3D cell images from the Allen WTC-11 collection in Appendix F . (a) Evaluation examples.

The fully supervised classifier is trained on the full microscopy training set and evaluated on the 59-category IID subset. For Cell-DINO ( Moutakanni et al., 2025 ) , we self-supervise the backbone on the same 2.5M microscopy training images and fit separate linear probes for structure and cell-line recognition; their predictions are combined for IID and Compositional Shift evaluation. CLIP ( Radford et al., 2021 ) , SigLIP ( Zhai et al., 2023 ) , SigLIP 2 ( Tschannen et al., 2025 ) , PE-Core ( Bolya et al., 2025 ) , and DFN2B-CLIP ( Fang et al., 2024 ) use released weights and native configurations, without microscopy adaptation or prompt ensembling. These comparisons measure direct transfer from general-purpose pretraining. Implementation details. MicroCLIP initializes both encoders from DFN2B-CLIP ViT-B/16 and fine-tunes all parameters with 224 × 224 224\times 224 image inputs and a 256-token text context. The training stream combines 2,505,017 microscopy images, 609,740 natural-image records, and 175,516 transformed copies of rare-class microscopy images.

We train for 12,000 updates using AdamW, a global batch size of 8,192, a peak learning rate of 4 × 10 − 5 4\times 10^{-5} , 2,500 warmup steps, cosine decay, and weight decay 0.2. Training uses bf16 mixed precision on eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 GPUs with 72 GB of memory each and takes approximately 55 hours. 6.2 Classification and Cross-Modal Retrieval Table 1 shows that MicroCLIP generalizes to unseen structure–cell-line pairings while maintaining high IID accuracy. It achieves 67.70% on Compositional Shift, compared with 5.12% for the strongest general-purpose VLM and 0.98% for Cell-DINO under factor-wise linear probing. On IID images, it reaches 98.46%, compared with 97.74% for the fully supervised classifier. Transfer also extends to held-out cell lines, structure labels, and an external source. MicroCLIP achieves 34.07% on Cell-Line Shift and 46.13% on Organelle-Set Shift, versus 7.63% and 2.54% for the strongest general-purpose baselines. Organelle-Set Shift concerns unseen complete labels, which may be composite, rather than necessarily unseen atomic structures. On Light My Cells ( Kauffmann et al., 2026 ) , MicroCLIP reaches 36.53%, versus 22.54% for PE-Core, although accuracy under distribution shift remains well below IID performance. The same representation supports retrieval with image-specific descriptions. On 1,000 held-out image–caption pairs with detail-level captions, MicroCLIP achieves 61.5% I2T and 63.3% T2I Recall@1, compared with at most 0.7% and 0.3% for the evaluated general-purpose VLMs. Table 1: Comparison of classification and cross-modal retrieval performance. MicroCLIP outperforms the evaluated general-purpose vision–language models in zero-shot structure–cell-line recognition and bidirectional retrieval, supporting language-guided analysis beyond training categories. Our evaluation is limited to these tasks in fluorescence microscopy, while broader biological targets and research tasks remain outside the scope of this study. Extending language-guided microscopy analysis to these settings is a promising direction toward a more general-purpose microscopy research assistant. AI use statement In this work, we used generative AI to generate synthetic text annotations for MicroPool-2M.

We also evaluated GPT-6 as a subject of study in the qualitative examples and classification diagnostic presented in Section 3 and Appendix D . We take full responsibility for the content of this work. Ethics Statement MicroPool-2M is constructed from existing microscopy resources and published data. We do not collect new human-subject data or personally identifiable information. Data provenance, preprocessing, and source-specific usage information are documented in the appendix and dataset documentation. Reproducibility Statement To support reproducibility, we describe the construction and evaluation splits of MicroPool-2M, as well as the MicroCLIP architecture, training configurations, and evaluation protocols, in the main text and appendix. We will publicly release MicroPool-2M, the MicroCLIP model weights, and training code to facilitate reproduction of the reported results. Results and scope. All runs use a 256-token text context. Classification is measured by Top-1 accuracy, with Source Shift evaluated on Light-My-Cells. Retrieval is measured by bidirectional Recall@1 on 1,000 held-out MicroPool image–text pairs with detail-level captions. The detail-only, knowledge-only, and category-plus-knowledge runs share the same training setup apart from their caption sampling ratios. The category-only and category-plus-detail runs use an earlier pipeline, while the three-level mix uses the full MicroCLIP training recipe. The single-level results reveal different performance profiles. Detail-only supervision reaches 48.10% I2T and 48.50% T2I Recall@1, but achieves only 56.53% IID and 26.53% Compositional Shift accuracy. Knowledge-only supervision also yields low classification accuracy and performs poorly on retrieval with detail-level captions.

Mixing category and knowledge captions raises IID accuracy from 39.95% to 97.47% and Compositional Shift accuracy from 12.08% to 63.17% relative to knowledge-only training. This comparison supports retaining direct category supervision for recognition. Classification uses category-name prototypes, so the single-level models trained without category captions also face a mismatch between training descriptions and evaluation text. The full MicroCLIP configuration samples category, detail, and knowledge captions with probabilities of 0.50, 0.25, and 0.25, respectively. It achieves the highest Compositional Shift accuracy, Cell-Line Shift accuracy, and retrieval Recall@1 among the reported configurations. It does not lead on every classification subset. Category-plus-detail supervision gives the highest IID and Source Shift accuracy, while category-plus-knowledge supervision performs best on Organelle-Set Shift. These results show that the full configuration combines strong recognition and retrieval performance, but the differences in training pipelines mean that its gains cannot be attributed to the sampling ratio alone.
